title: Neutron Star

description:
Episode 12 of a daily journey through the universe. ⭐

segments.text: Episode twelve. Next stop... a neutron star.
When a giant star explodes, its core can collapse into a ball just twenty kilometers wide, but heavier than our Sun.
segments.headline: Heavier than the Sun, 20 km wide

segments.text: It's so dense that one teaspoon of it would weigh about a billion tons.
Some spin over seven hundred times every second.
As they spin, beams of radiation sweep across space like a lighthouse. We call them pulsars.
segments.headline: Cosmic lighthouses

segments.text: Its gravity is so strong that the tallest mountains on its surface are less than a millimeter high.
segments.headline: Mountains under 1 mm

segments.text: And when two neutron stars crash together, they forge gold. Some of the gold on Earth may have been made this way.
segments.headline: Where gold comes from

segments.text: Tomorrow, we meet the strongest magnet in the universe. Next stop: a magnetar. Follow, so you don't miss episode thirteen.
